scope: Directed percolation in 1+1 dimensions: series expansions, critical point and exponent estimates, exact-form conjectures, competing numerical and field-theory methods, and experiments

sources.title: Low-density series expansions for directed percolation I: A new efficient algorithm with applications to the square lattice
sources.inspection: full text (arXiv v1, extracted with pdftotext; figure symbols in the update rules did not survive extraction)
sources.note: The current record and the reproduction target. Square bond series to order 171 and site series to order 158 for the moments of the pair connectedness. Non-nodal path-union transfer matrix, configuration growth about 2^(n/8), about 5.5 GB at order 171, residues modulo primes near 2^15 with up to 12 primes. Final estimates: bond p_c = 0.644700185(5), site p_c = 0.70548522(4), gamma = 2.277730(5), nu_par = 1.733847(6), nu_perp = 1.096854(4), beta = 0.276486(8) from scaling, Delta_1 consistent with 1.

sources.title: Low-density series expansions for directed percolation II: The square lattice with a wall
sources.inspection: primary abstract and HTML text via fetch summary
sources.note: Series to order 173 near an impenetrable wall. Surface exponents nu_par,1 = 1.733820(12), nu_perp,1 = 1.0968(1), gamma_1 = 1.82051(1). Scaling gives tau_1 = 1.00014(2), which appears to exclude the conjecture tau_1 = 1; the paper calls the value tantalizingly close and asks for a direct series for the average cluster length. This is the sharpest surviving exact-value question found.

sources.title: Low-density series expansions for directed percolation III. Some two-dimensional lattices
sources.inspection: primary abstract; table values from a fetch summary of the truncated HTML text
sources.note: Triangular bond 90 and site 82 terms, honeycomb bond 301, kagome 173/169, (4.8^2) 255/239. Exponents agree across lattices to the fifth digit. The square lattice was not extended. Reported p_c values (summary, not verified verbatim): triangular bond 0.47802525(5), kagome bond 0.65896910(8), (4.8^2) bond 0.76765116(7).

sources.title: Low-density series expansions for directed percolation IV. Temporal disorder
sources.note: Extends the same algorithm to temporally disordered DP. States that series were available by e-mail or from the author's Melbourne web page; that page is no longer reachable.

sources.title: Low-density series expansions for directed percolation on square and triangular lattices
sources.inspection: metadata; described in S01 section 2; DOI not verified
sources.note: The previous record: transfer matrix to t_max = 47 plus a correction-term extension procedure, reaching 112 terms (111 for mu_20). Earlier estimate p_c = 0.64470015(5). Volume and page from S01 reference 27; the link is a Crossref search because the DOI could not be verified.

sources.authors: Iwan Jensen and Anthony J. Guttmann
sources.title: Series expansions of the percolation probability for directed square and honeycomb lattices
sources.note: High-density series for the percolation probability P(q). Square bond q_c = 0.177143(2), beta = 0.2763(2). The first correction term is a Catalan number and higher corrections are rational functions of Catalan numbers, which drives the Baxter-Guttmann style extension. An independent observable for cross-checking beta.

sources.authors: Iwan Jensen and Anthony J. Guttmann
sources.title: Series expansions of the percolation probability on the directed triangular lattice
sources.note: Triangular bond and site P(q) series with Catalan-type correction formulas. Lattice cross-check for universality.

sources.authors: J. W. Essam, A. J. Guttmann and K. De'Bell
sources.title: On two-dimensional directed percolation
sources.note: Introduced the non-nodal resummation that doubles the series length (49 terms) and conjectured gamma = 41/18, nu_perp = 79/72, nu_par = 26/15. The S01 estimates exclude all three by many error bars.

sources.authors: R. J. Baxter and A. J. Guttmann
sources.title: Series expansion of the percolation probability for the directed square lattice
sources.note: Origin of the finite-lattice extrapolation idea used to extend series beyond the directly computed order. The DOI guessed earlier resolved to an unrelated paper, so the link is a Crossref search.

sources.title: Series expansions for the directed-bond percolation problem
sources.note: First transfer-matrix approach, 21 low-density terms, growth sqrt(2) per term. Useful low-order check values. Title not verified; link is a Crossref search.

sources.authors: J. W. Essam, K. De'Bell, J. Adler and F. M. Bhatti
sources.title: Analysis of extended series for bond percolation on the directed square lattice
sources.inspection: metadata verified via Crossref; cited as S01 reference 24
sources.note: 35-term series using a weak subgraph expansion. Low-order check values.

sources.authors: D. K. Arrowsmith and J. W. Essam
sources.title: Percolation theory on directed graphs
sources.inspection: metadata verified via Crossref; cited as S01 reference 29
sources.note: Source of the pair-connectedness expansion over unions of directed paths with weights d(g) = +-1, which is the basis of the S01 algorithm.

sources.title: Catalan numbers in a series expansion of the directed percolation probability on a square lattice
sources.inspection: bibliographic lead from reference lists; DOI not verified (link is a Crossref search)
sources.note: Exact structure in the correction terms of the P(q) series. Relevant to any claim of hidden exact structure, and possibly to checking computed coefficients.

sources.authors: M. Katori, N. Inui, G. Komatsu and K. Kameoka
sources.title: Hypergeometric series in a series expansion of the directed-bond percolation probability on the square lattice
sources.note: Follow-up to S13: higher correction terms written as hypergeometric series.

sources.title: New enumerative results on two-dimensional directed animals
sources.note: Directed-animal results used to derive leading correction terms in DP series. Exact combinatorics adjacent to DP.

sources.title: Haruspicy 3: The directed bond-animal generating function is not D-finite
sources.note: Proves the anisotropic directed bond-animal generating function is not D-finite, and so cannot be guessed by GFUN or differential approximants. Supports the expectation that DP is not D-finite; the method is a template for a non-D-finiteness argument.

sources.title: Equivalence of the two-dimensional directed-site animal problem to Baxter's hard-square lattice-gas model
sources.inspection: metadata from background knowledge; not retrieved this session
sources.note: Exact solution of directed animals, the classic example of hidden solvability next to DP. Background only.

sources.title: Equivalence of cellular automata to Ising models and directed percolation
sources.note: Domany-Kinzel cellular automaton, which contains bond DP via W(0|l,r) = (1-p)^(l+r) and the exactly solvable compact-DP line. Basis of the simple transfer matrix used for M0 checks.

sources.title: Asymptotic analysis of power-series expansions
sources.venue: Phase Transitions and Critical Phenomena, Vol. 13, eds. C. Domb and J. L. Lebowitz (Academic Press, 1989)
sources.note: Standard reference for differential approximants and ratio methods as used in S01.

sources.title: Series extension: predicting approximate series coefficients from a finite number of exact coefficients
sources.note: Differential approximants predict later coefficients well, and the predicted terms improve ratio-method estimates. Relevant to the M2 precision-gain projection and as a cheap complement to exact extension.

sources.title: Analysis of series expansions for non-algebraic singularities
sources.note: Methods for singularities outside the algebraic class. Background for interpreting the logarithmic singularity S01 finds on the negative axis of the bond series.

sources.title: Asymptotically faster algorithm for counting self-avoiding walks and self-avoiding polygons
sources.inspection: primary abstract and HTML text via fetch summary
sources.note: Improves transfer-matrix enumeration from exp(Cn) to exp(C sqrt(n log n)) in 2D, using pigeonhole over residue classes of cut columns plus inclusion-exclusion, for objects that are sparse. The author suggests it may generalize; whether DP path-union graphs are sparse in the required sense is an open question for M3.

sources.title: A parallel algorithm for the enumeration of self-avoiding polygons on the square lattice
sources.note: Parallel transfer-matrix design: the state vector is partitioned so that each task updates its own piece and data is redistributed when the update position moves across the partition. Template for multithreading and out-of-core streaming in M3.

sources.title: A new transfer-matrix algorithm for exact enumerations: self-avoiding polygons on the square lattice
sources.inspection: primary abstract and HTML text sections 1 to 2.2 via fetch agent
sources.note: Square-lattice self-avoiding polygons extended from 110 to 130 steps. Key change: instead of tracking how boundary edges are connected to the left (the past), the state records how they must be connected to the right (the future). Pruning then has a unique cheapest completion, and its cost drops from exponential in the width to O(W). The update rules become more complicated. This is the model for computing an exact per-configuration contribution order in the DP code (REVIEW section 10).

sources.title: D-algebraic guessing
sources.note: Guessing polynomial differential equations from finitely many terms. Possible tool for the M6 solvability tests beyond D-finite guessing.

sources.title: The art of algorithmic guessing in gfun
sources.note: Practical guide to guessing linear ODEs and recurrences (D-finite) from series. Tooling reference for M6.

sources.title: A new transfer-matrix algorithm for exact enumerations: self-avoiding walks on the square lattice
sources.note: Applies the M06 approach to walks. States that the gain comes from making it simple to calculate the order at which a configuration will contribute, at the cost of more complicated update rules.

sources.authors: Christian R. Scullard and Jesper Lykke Jacobsen
sources.title: Transfer matrix computation of generalised critical polynomials in percolation
sources.note: Critical-polynomial method for isotropic percolation thresholds, computed by transfer matrix. No application to directed percolation was found. The method relies on isotropic structure that DP lacks, so it is listed as a technique considered and set aside.

sources.title: High-precision percolation thresholds and Potts-model critical manifolds from graph polynomials
sources.note: Graph-polynomial thresholds to about 10 to 15 digits for 2D isotropic lattices. A benchmark for what large transfer-matrix computations achieve now, not a DP method.

sources.authors: A. Bostan, S. Boukraa, A. J. Guttmann, S. Hassani, I. Jensen, J.-M. Maillard and N. Zenine
sources.title: High order Fuchsian equations for the square lattice Ising model: chi-tilde^(5)
sources.venue: J. Phys. A 42, 275209 (2009) (DOI listed on arXiv)
sources.note: Found an order-33 Fuchsian ODE from a series computed modulo a single prime, without full CRT reconstruction. Template for testing DP series for D-finiteness directly from per-prime enumeration output. The Ising work used thousands of terms, so with about 250 DP terms only small ODEs can be excluded.

sources.authors: S. Boukraa, S. Hassani, I. Jensen, J.-M. Maillard and N. Zenine
sources.title: High order Fuchsian equations for the square lattice Ising model: chi^(6)
sources.venue: J. Phys. A 43, 115201 (2010) (DOI listed on arXiv)
sources.note: ODE factors guessed modulo several primes, then reconstructed in exact arithmetic. Shows the mod-prime-guess-then-lift workflow.

sources.authors: A. Bostan, F. Chyzak, G. Lecerf, B. Salvy and E. Schost
sources.title: Differential equations for algebraic functions
sources.inspection: metadata from background knowledge; not retrieved this session (link is a Crossref search)
sources.note: Source of the order-degree trade-off: a non-minimal-order ODE can have much lower degree, so fewer series terms are needed to guess it. Relevant to how many terms a D-finiteness test needs.

sources.title: Precise critical exponents for the basic contact process
sources.inspection: primary abstract and HTML text via fetch summary
sources.note: Exact diagonalization of the master operator for L up to 18 with Bulirsch-Stoer extrapolation: lambda_c = 1.64896(2), z = 1.58077(2), nu_perp = 1.09681(2), delta = 0.162(2). Within 1 to 2 of its own error bars of the S01 values, but 2 to 5 times less precise than series.

sources.authors: E. Carlon, M. Henkel and U. Schollwoeck
sources.title: Density matrix renormalization group and reaction-diffusion processes
sources.inspection: secondary description in the DMRG review cond-mat/0409292; venue from memory and not verified (link is a Crossref search)
sources.note: DMRG for 1D reaction-diffusion including the contact process, with exponents consistent with DP. Benchmark consumer of improved values.

sources.authors: Junfeng Wang, Zongzheng Zhou, Qingquan Liu, Timothy M. Garoni and Youjin Deng
sources.title: High-precision Monte Carlo study of directed percolation in (d+1) dimensions
sources.inspection: primary abstract; journal reference verified on arXiv
sources.note: Covers 2 <= d <= 7 only; 1+1 is left to series. Confirms that series is the reference method in 1+1.

sources.title: A transfer-matrix study of directed lattice animals and directed percolation on a square lattice
sources.note: Finite-strip transfer matrices give sequences of effective p_c and correlation-length exponent estimates. Numbers not retrieved; check precision against S01.

sources.title: Transverse-size critical exponent of directed percolation from Yang-Lee zeros of survival probability
sources.note: Strip transfer matrix for survival probability plus Yang-Lee zeros gives nu_perp and p_c precisely. Value not retrieved; it is the most recent dedicated 1+1 nu_perp estimate found.

sources.title: On directed interacting animals and directed percolation
sources.note: Strip transfer matrix linking interacting directed animals and DP. Precursor of N04.

sources.authors: Stephan M. Dammer, Silvio R. Dahmen and Haye Hinrichsen
sources.title: Directed percolation and the golden ratio
sources.inspection: primary abstract and HTML text via fetch summary
sources.note: Exact survival probability at unphysical complex p = 2 and p = (1 +- sqrt 5)/2. No exponent conjecture. Quotes beta = 0.27649(4) and p_c = 0.6447001(1) from Jensen 1996 PRL. Shows exact structure exists away from the physical critical point.

sources.title: A precise approximation for directed percolation in d=1+1
sources.inspection: primary abstract and HTML text via fetch summary
sources.note: Closure approximation giving p_c = (sqrt 5 - 1)/2 = 0.618 and beta = (1 - 1/sqrt 5)/2 = 0.276393. The beta differs from 0.276486(8) by about 12 error bars, so it is an approximation, not an exact value.

sources.title: High-precision simulations of the parity conserving directed percolation universality class in 1+1 dimensions
sources.note: Different universality class, but a recent model of how near-rational exponent claims are argued (beta = 1.000 and nu = 2 there, z not rational). Useful precedent for framing the M6 exact-form tests.

sources.title: Entropy governed by the absorbing state of directed percolation
sources.note: Tensor-network study of 1+1 DP. Its exponents are for entropy relaxation (delta_bond = 0.1593(1) etc.), not the standard set. A 2020 companion (arXiv 2008.10807) studies spectrum structure at criticality.

sources.authors: Shiwei Chen and Fa-Yueh Wu (per fetch summary)
sources.title: Directed percolation in two dimensions: An exact solution
sources.venue: Nankai Tracts in Mathematics vol. 10 (World Scientific, 2006), pp. 160-168
sources.note: Despite the title, solves a different row-alternating model whose criticality is in aspect ratio. Not a solution of square-lattice 1+1 DP; listed to prevent misreading.

sources.title: On the nonequilibrium phase transition in reaction-diffusion systems with an absorbing stationary state
sources.inspection: metadata from background knowledge; DOI not verified (link is a Crossref search)
sources.note: Half of the DP conjecture: generic absorbing-state transitions with a single absorbing state are DP. Background.

sources.title: On phase transitions in Schloegl's second model
sources.inspection: metadata from background knowledge; DOI not verified (link is a Crossref search)
sources.note: Other half of the Janssen-Grassberger DP conjecture. Background.

sources.authors: L. Ts. Adzhemyan, M. Hnatic, E. V. Ivanova, M. V. Kompaniets, T. Lucivjansky and L. Mizisin
sources.title: Field-theoretic analysis of directed percolation: Three-loop approximation
sources.inspection: primary abstract and HTML text via fetch summary; author list verified on arXiv
sources.note: All DP exponents to O(epsilon^3), epsilon = 4 - d. Not evaluated at d = 1 (epsilon = 3), where the truncated series is useless without resummation. A consumer of better 1+1 numbers as a resummation test.

sources.authors: M. Hnatic, M. Kecer, T. Lucivjansky and L. Mizisin
sources.title: Renormalization group analysis of directed percolation process: Towards multiloop calculation of scaling functions
sources.note: Extends the three-loop DP analysis to the equation of state. Indicates active field-theory interest in 2026.

sources.authors: L. Canet, B. Delamotte, O. Deloubriere and N. Wschebor
sources.title: Nonperturbative renormalization-group study of reaction-diffusion processes
sources.note: NPRG recovers DP exponents in low dimensions. Consumer of reference values.

sources.authors: N. Dupuis, L. Canet, A. Eichhorn, W. Metzner, J. M. Pawlowski, M. Tissier and N. Wschebor
sources.title: The nonperturbative functional renormalization group and its applications
sources.inspection: search snippet; author list from memory, not verified
sources.note: Review stating that DP exponents in d = 1, 2, 3 have been computed at LPA and LPA' and compare accurately with other methods. Points to the FRG d = 1 numbers to be tabulated in REVIEW.

sources.title: Background field functional renormalization group for absorbing state phase transitions
sources.note: FRG variant reporting good DP exponents even in low dimensions. Consumer of reference values.

sources.title: Bootstrapping nonequilibrium stochastic processes
sources.inspection: primary HTML text, first part verbatim and remainder via fetch summary
sources.note: Positivity bootstrap with LP and SDP gives rigorous bounds for the contact process and Domany-Kinzel model. Current bounds are loose (contact-process lambda_c >= 1.46 at L = 10 against 1.6489). Frames 1+1 DP as unsolved. A potential future consumer of reference values.

sources.authors: V. Brunel, K. Oerding and F. van Wijland
sources.title: Fermionic field theory for directed percolation in (1+1) dimensions
sources.inspection: search snippet; authors verified on arXiv
sources.note: An approximation scheme specific to d = 1. Example of a 1D-specific analytic approach that needs sharp benchmarks.

sources.title: On logarithmic extensions of local scale-invariance
sources.inspection: search snippet; metadata verified on arXiv
sources.note: Local scale invariance tested against transfer-matrix renormalization group data for the 1D critical contact process; the non-logarithmic form shows deviations (cond-mat/0603369). The tests are limited by how precisely DP exponents are known.

sources.authors: Ivan Balog, Hugues Chate, Bertrand Delamotte, Maroje Marohnic and Nicolas Wschebor
sources.title: Convergence of non-perturbative approximations to the renormalization group
sources.note: The derivative expansion of the functional RG, carried to high order, reaches conformal-bootstrap-level precision for the 3D Ising model. Makes precise 1+1 DP values more valuable as a target for the same programme applied to DP.

sources.authors: Gregoire Lemoult, Liang Shi, Kerstin Avila, Shreyas V. Jalikop, Marc Avila and Bjoern Hof
sources.title: Directed percolation phase transition to sustained turbulence in Couette flow
sources.inspection: search snippets; author list from memory, verify
sources.note: Quasi-1D circular Couette experiment, the main 1+1 DP realization in turbulence. Fitted exponent values not retrieved.

sources.authors: Liang Shi, Marc Avila and Bjoern Hof
sources.title: Scale invariance at the onset of turbulence in Couette flow
sources.note: beta = 0.29 +- 0.05 against the 1+1 DP value 0.276. Shows experimental precision is about two digits.

sources.authors: Gregoire Lemoult, Vasudevan Mukund, Hong-Yan Shih, Gaute Linga, Joachim Mathiesen, Nigel Goldenfeld and Bjoern Hof
sources.title: Directed percolation and puff jamming near the transition to pipe turbulence
sources.note: Pipe flow transition is in the DP class (effectively 1+1), with a jammed puff phase above criticality. Exponent values not retrieved.

sources.title: A universal transition to turbulence in channel flow
sources.note: Channel flow, 2+1 DP. Not a 1+1 test; listed to separate dimensionalities.

sources.authors: Kazumasa A. Takeuchi, Masafumi Kuroda, Hugues Chate and Masaki Sano
sources.title: Directed percolation criticality in turbulent liquid crystals
sources.note: The liquid-crystal experiment cited in the idea note. It is (2+1)-dimensional DP, not 1+1.

sources.authors: Kazumasa A. Takeuchi, Masafumi Kuroda, Hugues Chate and Masaki Sano
sources.title: Experimental realization of directed percolation criticality in turbulent liquid crystals
sources.note: Twelve exponents, five scaling functions and eight scaling relations, all 2+1 DP. Its comparison table lists earlier 1+1 experiments.

sources.title: Directed percolation describes lifetime and growth of turbulent puffs and slugs
sources.note: DP model of pipe-flow puff lifetimes and splitting, consistent with super-exponential lifetime data.

sources.title: Characterizing a non-equilibrium phase transition on a quantum computer
sources.note: Floquet quantum contact process on 73 trapped-ion qubits; data and simulations consistent with classical 1+1 DP. A recent consumer of reference exponents.

sources.title: Non-equilibrium critical phenomena and phase transitions into absorbing states
sources.note: Standard review. States that DP is one of very few critical phenomena whose 1+1 exponents are not known exactly, and that they do not seem rational.

sources.title: On possible experimental realizations of directed percolation
sources.note: Why DP was hard to observe experimentally before 2007. Context for the experiments section.

sources.title: Universality classes in nonequilibrium lattice systems
sources.note: Broad review of absorbing-state universality classes with exponent tables.

sources.title: Universal scaling behavior of non-equilibrium phase transitions
sources.note: Review with universal scaling functions and amplitude ratios for DP. Notes that DP exponents do not seem rational, unlike isotropic percolation.

sources.authors: Malte Henkel, Haye Hinrichsen and Sven Luebeck
sources.title: Non-Equilibrium Phase Transitions, Volume 1: Absorbing Phase Transitions
sources.inspection: metadata from background knowledge; not retrieved this session
sources.note: Textbook reference for DP scaling theory and exponent tables.

sources.authors: Hans-Karl Janssen and Uwe C. Taeuber
sources.title: The field theory approach to percolation processes
sources.note: Field-theory review for DP and dynamic isotropic percolation.
